visualReview.notes: Inspected seven final portable views. Three-bay black ground floor, nine cream-framed upper windows, extended central attic opening, cornice, hoist, set-back hipped canal roof, narrow link and transverse red annex roof match the recorded medium-fi exterior scope. Removed the draft neighboring rear building and corrected the front exposed gable. Plain party walls are intentional. Front step and foundations meet preserved source terrain.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected seven final shared viewer frames including north-up placement. Changed window surrounds and cornice from block-pattern masonry to smooth painted trim after the first material review. Shared brick and roof retain metric UV scale. The signed frame aligns the slim whole-house envelope and points the facade toward the canal. Flat fixture validates transforms and unloading; independent terrain appears in portable/context captures.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected nineteen final frames: twelve light/distance/mode combinations, front, back, silhouette and four forced detail levels. Authored skyline preserves front/link/annex shape and facade rhythm; district/street/closeup retain full source geometry within budget. No reduction tears or material popping were seen. Surrounding generic houses are synthetic style context, not Amsterdam parcels. Physical-device frame rates have not been measured.

The mapped 5.88 by 24.1 m envelope is partitioned approximately into front house, low/narrow connecting section and rear annex from the museum cutaway and inspected local architectural-model photo. Rear map feature 35184638705211 belongs to the neighbor and is excluded. Heading -120 degrees gives +Z northwest toward the canal. Preserved 4225 Terrarium samples are unmodified; front threshold [2.69,17.25] defines the 6.8055 m composite host datum. A -1 m foundation covers the -0.0123..0.2043 m local footprint relief. Generalized map geometry and coarse terrain are not surveyed measurements; footprint suppression remains off.

fidelityReview.scope: Original house at Prinsengracht 263, connecting section and annex exterior; adjacent houses and modern museum excluded.
fidelityReview.notes: Accepted as an original medium-fi exterior using two inspected local Qualla facade photographs, the local architectural-model photograph and museum historical cutaway. Recognizable frontage, black shopfront, cream window rhythm, white cornice, hoist and differing roof directions are represented. Hidden courtyard proportions and garden windows are interpretations rather than a measured current survey. Interiors, exact joinery and minor later alterations are outside scope. References are not embedded or redistributed.

limitations: Original medium-fi exterior, not a measured reconstruction. Facade follows local Qualla photos; the hidden courtyard/annex arrangement follows the museum historical cutaway and the local model photograph.
The zoom-15 map supplies a generalized 5.88 by 24.1 m envelope. Front/connector/annex partition and window/roof dimensions are estimates; small modern alterations and interiors are omitted.
Adjacent 261, 265 and the modern museum block are excluded. The former draft rear polygon was a neighboring property and has been removed.
Ground contact is reviewed against independently preserved coarse host-terrain samples; this is not elevation survey data. Reference images remain in Qualla and are not embedded in the asset.
